jobs.title: Senior Manager, Market Solutions Engineering
jobs.description:
The New York Independent System Operator (NYISO) manages the efficient flow of electricity on more than 11,000 circuit-miles of high-voltage transmission lines, dispatching power from hundreds of generating units across the state.

The New York Independent System Operator (NYISO) applies cutting-edge technology to operating a reliable electricity system, managing competitive markets for wholesale electricity, and planning for the Empire State's energy future. The NYISO’s Market Structures department invites applications for a full-time Senior Manager, Market Solutions Engineering.

The Senior Manager, Market Solutions Engineering is responsible for setting technical direction and leading the research, market technology, production support, implementation, and external engagement functions that support NYISO’s energy, capacity, and TCC market systems. This position provides strategic leadership across Market Design, Market Operations, Grid Operations, Market Mitigation and Analysis, Information Technology, System & Resource Planning, and Product and Project Management to advance NYISO’s strategic initiatives and long-term market vision.

The Senior Manager leads the development and evolution of market technology solutions, oversees preliminary and feasibility simulation studies for future market products, and ensures market applications remain functional and aligned with market rules and reliability criteria. The role also directs projects that build upon the Energy Market System and Business Market System to support emerging resource technologies and New York State renewable integration objectives.

The position provides leadership for day-ahead and real-time energy market engineering support, production issue resolution, vendor and consultant engagement, implementation readiness, testing coordination, external research engagements, and ongoing technical support for market software and market participant inquiries.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES And RESPONSIBILITIES

Provide strategic leadership for Market Solutions Engineering and Market Research and Engineering teams, including research, prototype development, market technology strategy, implementation support, production support, and long-term market solution planning.
Lead collaboration with Market Design, Project and Product Management, Information Technology, Operations, Grid Operations, Market Mitigation and Analysis, System & Resource Planning, and other business areas through the full project lifecycle, from market design and requirements development through implementation, testing, deployment, and post-production support.
Direct engagement with vendors and consultants supporting NYISO production systems and market applications; review vendor-proposed solutions, provide direction on design notes development and ensure solutions align with market rules, operational needs, reliability criteria, and long-range market strategies.
Provide strategic direction to Grid Operations and Market Operations teams regarding production changes, market software enhancements, prioritization of improvements, and resolution of software issues encountered in day-ahead and real-time market operations.
Define, sponsor and lead studies of future market products and technologies using prototyping, simulations, historical data analysis, and other sound technical approaches to validate requirements, assess technical robustness, evaluate potential market outcomes and consumer impacts, identify market behavioral risks and confirm compliance objectives.
Present, explain and defend technical approaches, study results, implementation strategies and recommended solutions to senior management, stakeholders, vendors, and internal cross-functional teams.
Balance market operations and grid operations operational enhancements with NYISO’s long-term market plans and strategic planning priorities.
Lead the technical development of mathematical models and optimization-based solutions for energy, capacity, and TCC markets, including commitment, dispatch, pricing, resource adequacy modeling approaches to meet peak system demand and capacity accreditation factors used in resource adequacy models.
Administer and provide direction on software modifications to Security Constrained Unit Commitment, Real-Time Scheduling, unit commitment, dispatch and pricing programs, including enhancements related to MIP solution approaches, dynamic reserves procurement, account for constraint-specific transmission shortages, modeling generator duct firing operational limitations, participation models for Energy Storage Resources, Co-located Storage Resources, aggregation resources, distributed energy resources, large load participation models in wholesale electricity markets, scarcity pricing enhancements, external transaction pricing, and broader regional market initiatives.
Lead or coordinate proof-of-concept testing, user acceptance testing and implementation readiness activities for changes to core energy market algorithms and supporting market software.
Provide implementation support to product teams by reviewing requirements documents, reviewing and approving design notes, supporting user acceptance test plans, and ensuring enhancements and new features are ready for production deployment.
Oversee technical support to Market Monitoring, IT Quality Assurance, Stakeholder Services, Market Validation, and Operations for market participant questions, scheduling and pricing outcome validation, production investigations, and audit-related inquiries.
Support corporate SOC1 process and procedure audit principles by promoting best practices, periodic audit activities, traceable documentation, and disciplined production-support processes.
Direct, support, and maintain specialized operations and market-solution applications, including PMU applications, stand-alone visualization software, as applicable to the assigned functional portfolio.
Monitor FERC, regional ISO/RTO, academia, and industry developments; collaborate with other ISOs/RTOs on technology and business solution evaluation; and recommend technical and business evolution initiatives in coordination with NYISO senior management.
Represent NYISO on external industry advisory boards and in industry organizations such as PSERC, EPRI, CEATI, CIGRE, national labs, universities, and other research forums; participate in major national and international conferences and seminars.
Oversee external research engagements for NYISO, including active management of university and research organization collaborations, review of DOE, NSF, NYSERDA, and related proposals, and maintenance of an active research program aligned with NYISO market needs.
Supervise, train, develop, and mentor managers and professional staff supporting market solutions, research, software testing, market modeling, and implementation activities; establish priorities, develop talent, and build technical depth across the team.
Provide direction for teams that provide 24x7 on-call production support to resolve issues in a timely manner.

Supervisory Responsibilities

This position has supervisory responsibility and may have both managerial and non-supervisory employees reporting to the position. The role is expected to provide leadership, coaching, prioritization, and performance direction for technical staff and subordinate leaders supporting market solutions, research, modeling, testing, implementation, and production-support activities.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations Research, or another related technical field is required. Knowledge of Power Systems Engineering and Economics is preferred. A Master’s degree is strongly preferred, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
A minimum of ten years of electrical engineering and/or software development experience is required, including technology leadership or supervisory experience in research, technology analysis, market systems, electric utilities, interconnected public service, or energy markets; or an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience.
Experience should include knowledge of power system operations, system planning, electricity markets, computer systems, optimization modeling, application software development, data engineering, scripting, and shell programming. For the senior manager role, demonstrated progressive leadership of complex market technology initiatives, cross-functional implementation teams, vendor relationships, external research engagements, and production support functions is expected.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

None required.

Additional Requirements

Excellent verbal, written, presentation, interpersonal, organizational, teamwork, and management skills.
Ability to read, analyze, and interpret scientific and technical journals, financial reports, legal documents, business periodicals, technical procedures, government regulations, and professional journals.
Ability to respond to inquiries or complaints from market participants, regulatory agencies, members of the business community, vendors, managers, and the public.
Ability to write reports, business correspondence, procedure manuals, speeches, articles, and materials that conform to prescribed style and format.
Ability to effectively present information to senior management, public groups, boards of directors, vendors, market participants, regulators, and cross-functional internal teams.
Ability to work with probability, statistical inference, advanced calculus, modern algebra, advanced statistical theory, geometry, trigonometry, optimization concepts, fractions, percentages, ratios, and proportions, and to apply these concepts to practical situations.
Ability to define problems, collect and analyze data, establish facts, draw valid conclusions, interpret complex technical instructions, and apply logical or scientific thinking to abstract and concrete problems.
Advanced competency in Linux operating systems, shell programming including Sed and Awk, scripting languages such as Python, optimization modeling primarily in AMPL or GAMS, and fine-tuning solution tolerances in commercial solvers such as Gurobi or CPLEX.
Intermediate competency in Windows operating environments using Microsoft Office applications, e-mail, and internet programs.
Knowledge and understanding of market software, market software development processes, IT software development practices, project lifecycle activities, and production support disciplines.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. The employee frequently is required to stand, walk, sit, and use hands to perform routine office tasks. The employee is occasionally required to reach with hands and arms. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 15 pounds. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate. Contact with staff and the public will occur. Travel may be required to attend and/or conduct meetings, conferences, and training. This position may require work on nights, weekends, or holidays.

At the NYISO, we realize the importance of balancing the availability of remote work with the inherent value of bringing people together to attain success in the areas of maximum collaboration, relationship building and growth, teamwork, innovation and problem solving, as well as professional development and mentoring. In this role, you will be required to work onsite from our Rensselaer, NY location several days per workweek, with the option to work remotely on the remaining days. You will also be expected to respond to all business needs that may require any increase to the regular onsite requirements.

This engagement offers an exceptional opportunity to conduct econometric forecasting and complex quantitative research in the heart of New York City. Partner with industry-leading technical experts to evaluate critical transportation, trade, and regional economic trends.

JOB TITLE

Economic Data Analyst - Fulltime - Hybrid

ROLE DETAILS

Location
: WTC, NYC
Work Mode
: Hybrid (3 to 4 days in-person)

COMPANY OVERVIEW

Toll International is a premier consulting firm based in New York City, specialized in comprehensive construction project management and technology-enabled solutions. Renowned for our dedication to delivering high-quality, cost-effective, and innovative results tailored to the unique needs of our clients, we lead infrastructure and digital transformation projects across New York State and beyond.
We are proud to partner with the Port Authority of New York & New Jersey (PANYNJ) on high-impact infrastructure and technology initiatives. We are currently seeking talented professionals to collaborate with subject matter experts, project managers, and process owners to deliver critical projects.

POSITION OVERVIEW

We are seeking a results-driven Economic Data Analyst to support quantitative research, data collection, and financial analysis for the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey. In this role, you will analyze large, complex datasets from key public economic sources to inform major agency initiatives, including capital plan inflation tracking, regional trade shifts, and remote work impacts. You will serve as a core technical resource, translating raw economic figures into actionable models and presentations.
Operating in a collaborative hybrid work environment, you will work closely with project managers, process owners, and interdisciplinary engineering teams. Your daily contributions will center on organizing data using rigorous best practices, executing literature reviews, and building clear econometric models in tools like R, Python, Excel, and Power BI. This position offers a direct platform to influence regional infrastructure policy while working at the iconic World Trade Center location.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Conduct quantitative, statistical, and qualitative analyses focused on the transportation sector and macroeconomic trends
Build and maintain econometric forecasting, benefit-cost, and economic impact models to support capital project decisions
Query, aggregate, and analyze large datasets from public economic databases including Census, USDOT, BLS, and FRED
Identify, model, and present critical economic trends, such as capital plan inflation impacts and changing regional remote work dynamics
Structure, clean, and organize complex data files using Excel best practices to ensure seamless knowledge transfer across teams
Automate repetitive data extraction and processing pipelines using programming languages such as R or Python
Create interactive dashboards, visual reports, and data queries using Power BI, Excel, and database systems
Monitor macroeconomic releases and market behavior, providing written commentary and literature reviews for executive leadership
Collaborate across multidisciplinary consultant and client teams in a hybrid office setting to present complex analytical findings clearly

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

Bachelor’s degree in Economics, Finance, Statistics, or a related field

3 or more years of professional work experience in economics, transportation, or the statistical domain

Demonstrated technical proficiency using Microsoft Excel, Power BI, Word, PowerPoint, and Access
Hands-on experience with analytical packages and statistical programming languages (R, Python, EViews, Stata, etc.)
Proven knowledge of foundational statistics, econometrics, and quantitative analysis methodologies
Demonstrated familiarity with major public data sources (Census, USDOT, BLS, FRED)
Ability to obtain a SWAC I.D. with associated security clearances immediately upon hiring

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

Master’s degree in Economics, Finance, Statistics, or a related field
Experience conducting capital plan inflation analyses or transportation activity analysis within a public agency environment

WHAT WE OFFER

Competitive salary with an extensive benefits package.
Engagement in high-profile, long-term projects.
A dynamic and supportive work environment.
Opportunities for professional growth and advancement.

What You Will Do

This position will be filled at either the Scientist 1 or Scientist 2 level, depending on the skills of the selected candidate. Additional job responsibilities (outlined below) will be assigned if the candidate is hired at the higher level.

The Manufacturing Focused Analysis Group (PAT-1) within the Associate Laboratory Directorate for Weapons Production (ALDWP) at Los Alamos National Laboratory is seeking highly motivated STEM professionals to support mission-critical manufacturing operations through advanced analytics, modeling, and decision-support tool development.

PAT-1 partners directly with stakeholders across Weapons Production to help leadership and program teams understand the current state of manufacturing and facility processes, quantify performance, and evaluate the impact of proposed changes. Our work enables informed decision-making that directly influences mission execution. Our team integrates engineering, data science, and operations research approaches to translate complex production environments into actionable insight. Core activities include:

Developing decision-support tools that synthesize production and facility data into meaningful metrics and visualizations
Processing, structuring, and analyzing large and diverse operational datasets
Designing and implementing discrete-event simulation models to evaluate process behavior and assess the effects of schedule, capacity, staffing, or infrastructure changes
Integrating analytics and modeling outputs into dashboards and executive-level reporting products
Collaborating with subject matter experts to define problem statements, validate assumptions, and ensure analytical rigor

In addition to our primary focus areas, PAT-1 contributes to emerging capabilities such as digital twin integration (including NVIDIA Omniverse environments), LiDAR data processing and spatial analysis, advanced visualization development, and enterprise dashboard solutions. These efforts support long-term modernization and enhanced situational awareness across production operations.

Successful candidates will work in a highly collaborative, cross-disciplinary environment composed of engineers, data scientists, and analysts from diverse technical backgrounds. Team members engage directly with manufacturing organizations and senior decision makers, translating technical analyses into clear, defensible recommendations that impact operational outcomes.

This position is suited for individuals who are motivated by solving complex, real-world problems; comfortable working with both data and stakeholders; and interested in applying STEM expertise to improve mission-critical manufacturing systems.

Demonstrated technical experience in a STEM discipline, as applied to projects spanning one or more of the following key areas of the group (data analytics, decision support, process improvement, simulation modeling and analysis).

The Data Analyst develops technical and conceptual skills over time under the mentorship of senior team members.

This position supports critical analysis of client data in support of scheduling and planning initiatives. The Data Analyst will become familiar with the types of data stored in student information systems and how Ad Astra consumes and processes that information. The person in this role is curious, detail-oriented, and resourceful in collaborating with colleagues to create reports, analyses, dashboards, and solutions, and applies a developing understanding of the role of analytics in supporting student success and degree velocity. Provide data entry support as needed, especially as it relates to pathways data.
Utilize AI, where possible, to streamline and improve data assessment and deliverable completion.
Collaborate with colleagues across Value and Insights, Consulting, Development and Product, and other teams to develop new reports and data visualizations.
Support the accurate import and interpretation of client data for consulting engagements, coordinating with clients and the Onboarding/Support team as questions arise.
